statement_original: Let $\phi(x),\Phi(x)$ be the probability density function (PDF) and the cumulative distribution function (CDF) respectively of the standard Gaussian distribution and denote $\bar{\Phi}(x) = 1 - \Phi(x)$. Let $\mathbf{1}_{d}$ be the vector of ones of dimension $d$. We use $\mathbb{1}{(\cdot)}$ to denote the indicator function of a set and $|\cdot|$ to denote the cardinality of a set. For two sets $A$ and $B$, denote their symmetric difference by $A \ominus B$, i.e., $A \ominus B = (A\setminus B) \cup (B\setminus A)$; let $A \times B$ be the Cartesian product. For two positive sequences $\{x_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ and $\{y_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$, we say $x_n = O\left(y_n\right)$ if $x_n\le C y_n$ holds for any $n$ with some large enough $C>0$. And we say $x_n = o\left(y_n\right)$ if $x_n/y_n  \rightarrow 0$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$. For a sequence of random variables $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ and a scalar $a$, we say $X_n  \le a + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ if for all $\epsilon > 0$, $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{P}\left({ X_n - a > \epsilon }\right) = 0$. Given a random variable $Z$, we define its $\psi_{\ell}$-norm for $\ell \ge 1$ as $\|Z\|_{\psi_{\ell}} = \sup_{p \ge 1} p^{-1/\ell} (\mathbb{E}|Z|^p)^{1/p}$. Let $[d]$ denote the set $\{1,\dots,d\}$. The $\ell_{\infty}$ norm and the $\ell_{1}$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^d$ are denoted by $||\cdot||_{\infty}$ and $||\cdot||_1$ respectively. For a random vector $X$, let $||X||_{\infty}$ be its $\ell_{\infty}$ norm. For a matrix $\mathbf{A}\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$, we denote its minimal and maximal eigenvalues by $\lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{A}), \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{A})$ respectively, the elementwise max norm by $\left\|\mathbf{A}\right\|_{\max} = \max_{i\in [d_1],j\in [d_2]}|\mathbf{A}_{ij}|$ and the elementwise $\ell_0$ norm by $\left\|\mathbf{A}\right\|_{0} = \sum_{i\in [d_1],j\in [d_2]}\mathbb{1}{(\mathbf{A}_{ij} \ne 0)}$. Throughout this paper, $C, C',C'', C_0, C_1, C_2,\dots$ are used as generic constants whose values may vary across different places.
